decisions.name: (4.2.6) Proposition
decisions.reason: Extension of every character of an abelian normal subgroup in a split group is the extension-construction step of the next page, not required for an assumed extension in Gallagher.
decisions.evidence: The current RG-4 manifest states Gallagher only under an assumed extension, while current RG-5 (order 510.039) is the designated extension-construction page.

decisions.name: Remark 15.13(1)
decisions.reason: Quasiparabolic subgroups and the B2 counterexample address root-coset stabilizers, not the reflection-generated definition consumed here; no parabolicity or closed-subsystem assertion is made.
decisions.evidence: The current RL-4 manifest uses reflection linkage and makes no quasiparabolic, closed-subsystem, or root-coset-stabilizer assertion.

decisions.name: Remark 1.5 (More on projective representations), (b)
decisions.reason: Twisted group algebra modules encode a nontrivial factor set and are explicitly assigned to the next page; all algebras used here are ordinary group algebras.
decisions.evidence: The current RG-4 manifest uses only ordinary group algebras; current RG-5 explicitly introduces factor sets and projective representations.

decisions.name: Corollary 20.10
decisions.reason: Injective hulls are duals of projective covers; projective-cover existence is the next pair’s central construction and is not needed for restricted duality itself.
decisions.evidence: The current RL-4 manifest proves restricted duality without injective hulls; current RL-5 design begins the projective-cover and injective development.

decisions.name: Remark 15.10
decisions.reason: The A3 example separates root order from strong linkage, a distinction established on the preceding linkage pair; its additional rank-three arithmetic is not needed for category O finiteness or blocks.
decisions.evidence: The current RL-4 manifest does not use the rank-three root-order example; its linkage dependencies are the earlier RL-3 statements.

decisions.name: Remark 1.5 (More on projective representations), (a)
decisions.reason: Rephasing a projective representation changes its factor set by a coboundary; this is needed for the next page obstruction class, not for an existing linear extension.
decisions.evidence: The current RG-4 manifest has no projective multiplier or rephasing claim; current RG-5 is expressly the factor-set and coboundary page.

decisions.name: (4.2.7) Remark
decisions.reason: Classification for split abelian normal subgroups is precisely the next page little-group method; ordinary Clifford and Gallagher here provide its prerequisites.
decisions.evidence: The current RG-4 route stops at ordinary Clifford and assumed-extension Gallagher; current RG-5 is the planned little-group classification page.

decisions.name: 15.4. The stabilizer in W of a point in h*/Q / Proposition 15.12
decisions.reason: The equality of the root-lattice coset stabilizer with the reflection-generated subgroup is stronger than the block theorem needs here. The scaffold proves block separation using simple extensions and strong linkage, without invoking this affine-Weyl/CST result.
decisions.evidence: The current RL-4 block theorem is routed through simple extensions and strong linkage, not the stronger affine-Weyl root-lattice-coset stabilizer equality.

decisions.name: Equivalence of blocks with a fixed central character (unnumbered paragraph)
decisions.reason: Categorical equivalence of distinct nonintegral blocks via localization is stronger than decomposition and uses localization techniques absent from this pair; no subsequent argument here consumes it.
decisions.evidence: The current RL-4 manifest asserts decomposition by generalized central character and linkage blocks only; it contains no localization-based equivalence of distinct blocks.

decisions.name: Exercise 15.5
decisions.reason: The Harish-Chandra (g,K)-module variant belongs to analytic representation theory and supplies no prerequisite for the algebraic category O proofs.
decisions.evidence: The current RL-4 manifest is algebraic category O and carries no Harish-Chandra (g,K)-module assertion or dependency.

decisions.name: Definition 1.4
decisions.reason: Projective representations, similarity and irreducibility are definitions assigned to the next projective-extension page; ordinary linear extension theory here does not require them.
decisions.evidence: The current RG-4 manifest has an ordinary linear extension definition for Gallagher; current RG-5 explicitly introduces projective representations and factor sets.

decisions.name: Remark 3.18
decisions.reason: The Verdier-duality and Kazhdan–Lusztig geometric interpretation requires the geometric representation theory apparatus and is not load-bearing for this algebraic restricted duality construction.
decisions.evidence: The current RL-4 restricted-duality construction is algebraic and has no Verdier-duality or Kazhdan-Lusztig geometric claim.

decisions.name: Lemma 3.14
decisions.reason: Standard–costandard Hom orthogonality is part of the next pair’s combined Hom/Ext vanishing item used to prove BGG reciprocity; the present duality proof does not require it.
decisions.evidence: The current RL-5 design explicitly owns standard-costandard Hom/Ext vanishing for BGG reciprocity; no RL-4 item depends on it.

decisions.name: Theorem 1.3, final generalized tensor-product clause
decisions.reason: The character-triple tensor generalization is beyond the assigned quotient Gallagher result. As printed it reuses chi as an extension of theta while mapping Irr(G|theta) to Irr(G|tau theta), an inconsistent parameter choice; this clause is not used as a mathematical premise.
decisions.evidence: The current RG-4 manifest states the quotient Gallagher correspondence only and does not import the source's generalized character-triple clause.

decisions.name: 2-cocycles, 2-coboundaries and H2 (unnumbered after Definition 1.4)
decisions.reason: The factor-set equivalence and obstruction class belong to the next page. Its cohomology-versus-homological-Schur-multiplier convention must be resolved there, not imported into ordinary Clifford theory.
decisions.evidence: The current RG-5 design owns two-cocycles, coboundaries, and the obstruction-class convention; current RG-4 has no cohomological claim.

decisions.name: Remark 3.15
decisions.reason: Derived orthogonality introduces the higher Ext interface for standard/costandard objects; it is deferred together with that pair’s Hom/Ext vanishing development.
decisions.evidence: The current RL-5 design owns the higher Ext interface in its standard-costandard vanishing item; current RL-4 contains no derived assertion.

decisions.name: Lemma 3.16
decisions.reason: The standard–costandard Ext1 splitting proof is read completely, but belongs with the next pair’s standard/costandard Hom and Ext vanishing result.
decisions.evidence: The current RL-5 design owns standard-costandard Ext1 splitting within its Hom/Ext vanishing development; current RL-4 has no dependency on it.

decisions.name: Remark 15.13(2)
decisions.reason: The dual-group centralizer interpretation is additional algebraic-group geometry and has no role in the extension/duality proof of linkage blocks.
decisions.evidence: The current RL-4 manifest uses no dual-group centralizer interpretation and asserts only the algebraic linkage-block decomposition required by its route.
